disease_label_per_paper: Extensive invasive pulmonary aspergillosis after short-course steroid therapy for asthma/bronchitis
paper_diagnosis_source_text_value: We describe the case of an elderly woman who was found to have extensive IPA, in the absence of classic risk factors.
presentation_summary: Shortness of breath and malaise after bronchitis treatment with inhaled steroids, antibiotics, oral prednisone, and levofloxacin.
One week before admission she had fever, chills, wheezing, and cough with yellow sputum, but she was afebrile with normal room-air oxygen saturation in the emergency department.
Admission labs showed leukopenia, anemia, CKD-range creatinine and BUN, and normal initial chest radiograph.
CT evolved from bilateral multifocal ground-glass opacities to extensive bilateral nodular infiltrates with ground-glass opacities.
Aspergillus was found in sputum cytology and autopsy showed bronchial mucosal invasion and vascular invasion with pulmonary arterial thrombi.
